traps.why: I₂ couples two thiols into a disulfide; for a sulfide you need the thiolate plus an alkyl halide.
There is a reaction: 1. NaOH; 2. CH₃I does change ethanethiol.

explanation: NaOH deprotonates the thiol (pKa ≈ 10) to the thiolate, which does SN2 on the CH₃/1° halide: a sulfide (thioether).

flaws.why: Step 1 (CH₃I) does nothing here: A neutral thiol is a poor nucleophile here; make the thiolate first (NaOH or NaOEt).
